about.title: Red Bluff Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, but the aftermath in Red Bluff often drags on for weeks — medical visits, missed shifts, and a property owner who won't return your calls. Whether the fall happened along Antelope Boulevard at a retail center, in a grocery store off Walnut Street, or on a poorly lit stairwell near Main Street, California law asks a specific question: did the property owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard, and did they fail to fix it or warn you? That's the heart of a premises liability claim. Because Red Bluff sits in Tehama County and many properties are privately owned, claims here usually move faster than ones involving public buildings, which carry a much shorter reporting window. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect you with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, help you gather evidence before it disappears, and explain your options at no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Red Bluff Fall

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires proof that the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help identify inspection logs, prior complaints, or repair records that establish that knowledge.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Red Bluff businesses and apartment complexes overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having nothing.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover even if you're partly responsible for the fall. An attorney can help present the facts so your share of fault is assessed fairly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Red Bluff?
items.answer: In most cases against a private property owner, California gives you two years from the date of the fall. If the fall happened on public property, such as a Tehama County building or sidewalk, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. It's worth talking to an attorney as soon as possible to avoid missing a cutoff.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my own fall?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still pursue a claim even if you weren't paying full attention when you fell. Your potential recovery may be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't eliminated. An attorney can help gather evidence that accurately reflects what happened.

items.question: Does it matter that my fall happened at a busy time, like a Friday afternoon?
items.answer: It can. Public crash data shows Red Bluff traffic incidents often cluster on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m., and busy periods at stores or public spaces near corridors like Main Street or Antelope Boulevard can mean hazards go unnoticed longer. Documenting the time and conditions of your fall helps establish how long a hazard may have existed.

items.question: Do I have to pay anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. You can ask questions and learn your options with no upfront cost.
